beta_new: Begin up a black stain, latch hold of a high ledge, then rock onto the slopers. Ten feet of slopey pinches follow, then you shift rightward onto a jug, and pockets lead through the groove above to the anchors.
Climb the corner crack to a ledge, then rappel, or link into the upper pitch of the neighbouring Groundhog to gain the top.
The blank lower face leads to a hand-sized ledge around fifteen feet off the ground; above, cross another horizontal break on the vertical face and finish at the anchors.
Start by the arete and haul yourself over the jugs of the bulge to reach the anchor.
Tricams are the key protection on this face just left of a neighbouring route. The anchors of the next route over also allow a top rope.

moves.from: Tricams are the key protection on this face just left of a neighbouring route.

beta_new: Slap your way along the rounded arete, then work out leftward near the top; the final stretch is straight up on crimps to the anchors.

A delicate opening gets you to a good stance by the hueco's left side. Then tiptoe off leftward across the face, where holds disappear; after a handful of slender moves they grow large again, and you cruise to the chains.
Start directly below the first bolt with a slopey left-hand crimp then a sidepull, then rise onto your feet and trace the evident line up to the anchors.

A few feet of ledges lead to a crescent-shaped jug, then small pockets and edges carry you to bolt two. Two opposing jugs follow, and the route is about hanging on as long as possible, ideally to the anchors.
Head directly up the face of pockets, passing a huge cave-like hueco on its left side partway up. Pull a small roof, then slant upward, drifting a little right to the chains.
Enjoyable moves open the route, then you teeter up the sturdy sandstone using decent edges, all the way to the chains.
Boulder to the first bolt, then wade up the jugs on the longer overhanging wall to the anchor.

Race through the opening bolts, then lunge out right to a jug. After a shake, go left via pockets and then up, stringing together one-after-another moves between slopers and edges; keep something in reserve for the last pull before the anchors.
Follow the hand-size crack in the corner as far as a ledge, then shuffle right to a tree for the rappel.
Latch a low shelf to haul into the meat of the route, then crank across gastons and pinches the rest of the way to the anchors.
Get through a dirty opening, then crank stretched-out moves and a pair of fingerlocks to reach the lower anchors; the line carries on to a second set above.

Ascend until the roof blocks you, then traverse rightward by hand for ten to fifteen feet to reach a hand crack. Place gear, then crank up the crack as it thins and steepens until a decent ledge appears. Clip the bolt, lunge for the jug, and crimp to the anchors.
Follow the neighbouring route's start to the hueco, go right and work a handful of delicate moves, then sprint up big jugs to the chains.
Work through the sequences of the lower wall until you reach a decent stance, and use that pause to plan the boulder problem waiting just under the chains.

Climb the offwidth to begin, then escape sideways onto the wall, relying on small footholds and fingertips. Continue on crimps and edges, and when it suits you, traverse left onto the finishing bolts of the neighbouring route.
A lunge to a jug starts things off; after that the bolted face continues past the overlap about fifty feet up.
Very technical moves lead up this less-than-vertical line, and a little roof guards the anchors.
Trend rightward after the first bolt toward the crack until you reach a ledge, surmount the little overhang, then climb on plates up to the chain anchors.
Share the start of the neighbouring route, then angle away to the left: pull its entrance moves, then traverse left to a big undercling by the second bolt.

Pockets lead past a creaky, juggy flake near the ground and onward to a horizontal ledge-line. The face then looks blank; aim for another shelf, then a lumpy iron-coloured jug around mid-height, and finish beneath a wavy break below the chain anchor.
The thin crack leads to a ledge beneath the roof. Reach out from the ledge to place gear in the roof, then spring up into it and fight your way over the lip.
Clip your way through the first trio of bolts on the neighbouring route, then branch off along the slender seam, where a wickedly hard boulder problem awaits.
Squirm up the corner as a chimney. Gear is minimal: one tiny cam or a single stopper fits around a third of the way up.

moves.from: Gear is minimal: one tiny cam or a single stopper fits around a third of the way up.

value.text: One tiny cam or a single stopper.

moves.from: Finish on top, or come down from the neighbouring route's anchors.

beta_new: Haul on plates to gain the slab, then work the vertical section, where a tricky move gets you to the following bolt. Larger holds lead the rest of the way.
Stretch for the opening hold, then follow the flake as it angles left, placing hand-size gear along the way.
Pick the right-hand crack of the pair splitting a blocky yellow-and-black corner; a flared little roof near the summit caps it, and you finish by lowering off fixed gear.
Climb the slab, following five bolts as the face thins into a pocketed, bouldery stretch. The overhanging finish brings surprisingly good holds.

Start from a small ledge and work the technical, concave face using edges and tiny pockets. Once the wall steepens, slopers and jugs take over, and keep some energy for the thrilling moves just below the anchors.
Climb the short, thin finger crack, step into the dihedral above, then work a hand-over-hand shuffle, slaps and crimps to the anchors.
Work the delicate opening, then surge past the early bolts on strong slopers and underclings. Lower off the first anchors if time is short, or keep going on much easier ground to the top anchors.
Pockets lead to a pointed brown shelf where you can shake out, then more pockets carry you to the anchors.
Pass the block on either side and move into the cave. Leaving it, either finish via an offwidth to a ledge, or shuffle leftward beneath a roof, reaching the anchors of a neighbouring route.
Ascend the lower face to a solid resting spot just short of where the wall tips steep, then fight your way through the steep section, keeping some energy for the roof beneath the anchors.
Combine the thin seam with the holds around it to boulder your way onto the ledge, then lower off the bolted anchors.
A brief bouldery section on grainy, slopey stone leads to some good sidepulls. After clipping bolt two, muscle past some pockets and pinches, arriving on easier, mossy terrain.
